what_happened: Reproduced the exact reported silent-exit signature (mode line then exit 1, no reason) with a minimal script mirroring git-snapshot.sh's --no-revert branch under a held .git/index.lock; confirmed git stash create fails with status 1 and set -e aborts the unguarded STASH_SHA=$(...) assignment before any reason is printed. Also confirmed via a 2000-entry stash fixture that the sibling STASH_REF=$(git stash list | head -1 | cut -d: -f1) pipeline independently fails under pipefail/SIGPIPE once stash-list output is large, in both --no-revert and default mode (line 501 shares the identical unguarded shape).

context/standards/shell-strict-mode.md's Class A set -euo pipefail migration audit explicitly lists scripts/git-snapshot.sh under 'Phase 7 remainder (core)' and asserts for that population 'None found unguarded ... every conditional read is already inside if/||/&&, or reads via 2>/dev/null || true / 2>/dev/null || echo <default>'. This is contradicted by reproducible evidence: git-snapshot.sh lines 442, 464, 471, 479, and 501 are command substitutions assigning from a git (or git-piped) command with a bare 2>/dev/null and no || fallback, none wrapped in if/||/&&. The audit's own admission-test checklist (bare non-if-guarded command chains) should have caught these; worth a follow-up correction to that doc once this task's fix lands.

The research report's Decisions section rules that a --no-revert stash-create failure should DEGRADE to a warning and continue (exit 0), but its own Recommendation 4 then specifies the acceptance fixture must assert 'a non-zero, documented exit status' for the held-index.lock case. The two are mutually exclusive. Resolved at plan time in favour of the Decisions ruling: the fixture asserts exit 0 plus a named WARNING on stderr plus patch/marker still written, and 'documented exit status' is satisfied by documenting that status in the script header rather than by requiring non-zero.

Built a 2000-entry SIGPIPE fixture in ~12s via git stash create (distinct commit per differing message) plus git update-ref --create-reflog, after discovering git update-ref silently no-ops (no reflog entry appended) when old==new SHA -- avoided a much slower per-entry git stash push cycle.

Plan Phase 4's verification criterion names verify-deploy.sh gate 3 (doc-lint) as expected green at Phase 4 time, but gate 3's deployed-script-content-drift sub-check cannot pass until after Phase 5's redeploy by construction (source changed in Phases 2-3, deploy regenerates in Phase 5). Confirmed via direct check-extension-docs.sh run that the only FAIL lines attributable to this task's own files are drift-only (scripts/git-snapshot.sh, scripts/tests/test-git-snapshot.sh), not a content/structure defect in the new header text; gate 4 (task-reference lint) was run standalone and PASSED cleanly. Deferred re-verification of gate 3 to Phase 5 after redeploy.

verify-deploy.sh gate 13 (whole-tree orphan detection) flagged .claude/tmp/stash-pre-<this-session-id> as an orphan during Phase 5's full gate run. Root cause: sibling task 382's guard-destructive-git.sh PreToolUse hook (its stash-provenance-lib.sh) intercepts any Bash call whose text contains 'git stash' and snapshots the current repo's stash list under .claude/tmp/, regardless of whether the command targets a scoped throwaway fixture repo elsewhere (-C <dir>) -- it ran against this repo's own stash list during this task's SIGPIPE-fixture test runs. Unrelated to git-snapshot.sh or test-git-snapshot.sh (neither is in task 382's declared file_scope and this file is gitignored runtime state under the fully-gitignored .claude/ tree, not a tracked deliverable). Deleted the stray file to unblock this task's own gate-13 verification; task 382's hook will recreate state files as needed on its own future runs.

Task 386's postflight completion write was refused by the completion-deploy gate (exit 6): the deployed .claude/ tree was stale relative to the source store at completion time. Deferred to the next cycle's Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint to deploy and reconcile.
